newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Milling wheat, barley up, maize mixed in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Milling wheat, barley up, maize mixed in Hungary.

text.p: Milling wheat futures gained on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday on buying interest, dealers said.
"The May maturity rose entirely on one brokerage's purchases," said Istvan Grebats of Termin.
May, October and December milling wheat rose by the daily 400-forint limit to end at 24,100 forints per tonne for May, 22,250 for October and 23,000 for December.
Thursday's news that the government was getting close to striking a barter deal with Bulgaria for the export of some 20,000 tonnes had no impact on the market, Grebats said.
"The market remained unimpressed," he said. "This delivery would probably come from the state's reserves, which currently stand at 200,000 tonnes."
He said rising wheat prices in Chicago were the other factor supporting the Hungarian price increases.
The rise affected barley, despite a lack of demand for feed.
"I think livehog and chicken numbers are down maybe 20 percent on last year, so there is a diminishing demand for feed," Grebats said.
Shrinking livestock numbers would probably have a more significant impact on maize prices, he added.
On Thursday, maize prices rose for July by 10 forints to end at 17,510 and dropped 350 forints for December to close at 18,650.
Trade in maize futures was very light.
Total grains futures turnover was 189.5 million forints, up from Wednesday's 63.5 million but still below average. Milling wheat accounted for 337 contracts out of a total 422 traded.
